reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30-40 feet over brush with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: If you like to livescope offshore bass can be target with an umbrella rig, and a minnow on a jig head. Shallow bass can be caught with a weightless 5 inch stick bait in shad and bluegill patterns around docks. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Before the cool down, we were using Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs vertically with a slow upward retrieve.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Mornings bass bite continues to be slow on chatterbaits and spinnerbaits in 2-5 feet. Crappie are slow in the creek channels in 30-50 feet of water on timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Black bass, stripers, and catfish remain slow, with minimal activity reported.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4 pounds are slow on all-around jigs, shallow crankbaits on the rocks and docks, and with 5-7 inch minnow style baits scoping main lake pockets suspended over 18-25 feet. Crappie are excellent to 1.75 pounds on minnows, pink and yellow or shad colored jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles, or shooting jigs under docks in 18-22 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in standing timber suspended 25-30 feet down with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: This disrupted the winter bass pattern, but now that cold nights have returned the water temperature should drop to back into the low to mid 50s. Crappie are good in the same area.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers remain slow, with limited action across the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: There are also some good groups of large white bass and small largemouth schooled up toward the river. The largemouth fishing has also been good with the warmer days. Bass can be caught on the outside edge of the hydrilla deadsticking a weighted wacky rig.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing has been excellent, with good reports of blue and channel catfish, as well as black bass and white bass being caught.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass remain active offshore, chasing shad schools and pushing onto shallower areas. Crappie have been productive on structure in 13-24 feet, with hair jigs producing best, though plastics and minnows also work. Hybrid stripers are being caught in good numbers on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad, with a few taken dead-sticking in 17-33 feet; dead-sticking should improve as water temperatures drop.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been slow for bass after the cold front, and high winds have limited angler activity.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with fish scattered in shallow water biting rattle traps, chatterbaits, and Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fork crappie fishing is finally in a wintertime pattern. You can find large schools of crappie congregating on timber along creek channels in 35-60 feet of water. The winter bite on Lake Fork is the best time of year to catch a limit of crappie quickly and even catch some giant crappie mixed in with the eater size fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacking up on structures in 15-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting in 4-6 feet of water with white crankbaits or white rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14-16 feet on brush with minnows and jigs. Bass are good around main lake points with slow moving baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Fishing reports have been slow to fair for most species except for crappie. Crappie are good near submerged structures when baitfish are holding. Crappie can be caught slowly working small jigs. The best crappie action is in town and upstream. Largemouth bass are good on main lake points and near major creek entrances on soft plastics worked near drop-offs. Largemouth bass to 6 pounds are possible when located. Some largemouth are being caught mixed in with the striped bass in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Texas-rigged worms and green Rage Craws around points, drop-offs, and cypress knees, and squarebill crankbaits in pilchard patterns diving 3-5 feet are producing along riprap. Catfish are active near the train tracks and in the West Fork on fresh shad kept on ice, while crappie are making a solid return with good limits coming from brush piles in 8-12 feet of water in Luce Bayou and the East Fork on hand-tied jigs or minnows. White bass action remains strong on the south end by trolling a 25-foot diver with a 3-foot leader and #12 Pet Spoon at 2.6-2.9 miles per hour in about 14 feet of water, with slabs and crankbaits also working near the West Fork.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along the bank and on boat docks with jigs, soft plastics, crankbaits, and swimbaits. There are some deep bass chasing shad, and can be caught on Alabama rigs, swimbaits and jerkbaits

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass can be caught in 5-10 feet near deep water on crankbaits. Crappie are in brush piles. Bass are related to bait and the bait has slid out to the mid depth up to 25 feet over major structure changes. The bass bite has been a little slow in the mornings but picking up in the afternoon. Shad color crankbaits are working, and it may be time to pull out the Alabama rig and go after the bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very good on jigs or minnows. Crappie can be found in 30 feet of water suspended at 22-24 feet on trees. Bass have slowed down some but can still be found on structure in 10-15 feet of water. Jigs, crankbaits and jerkbaits fished in and over brush piles along the 10-15 feet on structure lines have taken the best bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Any rock around the lake has been able to produce some bass bites on shad imitating baits. Also, there are schools of bass chasing around balls of shad.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: White bass, catfish and crappie are roaming fish in 18-24 feet of water. Crappie are on brush, roaming, and on the power line pylons biting minnows. Crappie eggs are still not fully developed yet. Largemouth bass are in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Fishing is productive for a variety of species: white bass are actively chasing shad in open water and creeks, with slabs and spoons working best in 10-25 feet. Largemouth bass can be found around wood, brush, and grass edges using plastics, crankbaits, and spinnerbaits. And while crappie and striped bass are present, they are less consistent, with crappie on deeper structure and stripers following bait or current.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing bait balls.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good to excellent in deep water with Carolina rigs and deep crankbaits around fallen timber in 15-25 feet of water, or shallow around hydrilla with lipless crankbaits, chatterbaits, swimbaits, senkos and flukes. Crappie are scattered across the lake in standing timber at multiple depths. Sand bass can be found from the cool water intake to the hot water discharge using tail spinners and slab spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with a Colorado bladed spinnerbait on main lake points in 5 feet of water or a shallow diving crankbait. Crappie are excellent on chartreuse and black crappie jigs on a split shot rig or live minnows. Crappie are deep and suspended on timber, so it is best to timber hop with live-scope.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on suspended jerkbaits and small swimbaits on creek channel swings. Crappie are excellent grouped up standing timber with white or chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations are strong, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are fair suspended jerkbaits and Alabama rigs. Crappie are fair grouped up standing timber with white or chartreuse crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with numbers of fish up to 4 pounds caught, and some up to 10 pounds possible. Crappie are slow on minnows in front of the Game Warden Cove.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in deep water with minnows. Black bass, hybrids and sand bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good suspending jerkbaits or small swimbaits in shallow water. Crappie are good on deep brush piles with white and clear crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been slow to fair with the occasional good day. Crappie are fair to good under docks. Largemouth are good using a slow approach in the cold water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can still be caught shallow around dock poles and rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina the crappie bite is fair, and catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows holding tight under brush in 8-16 feet of water or roaming. Black bass are slow on craw jigs and slow plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Before the cool down, we were using Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs vertically with a slow upward retrieve. Largemouth continue to be good on white or silver three-quarter ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs worked with a snap jigging tactic around deep timber.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are holding steady on structure in 15-20 feet of water as the water is holding consistently in the 55 degree range.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good targeting ledges in 20-30 feet of water with Texas rigs or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with fish scattered on brush piles in 16-20 feet of water with minnows. Bass are slow in 8-10 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have transitioned to the winter pattern. Black bass can be caught while targeting crappie. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow to fair at the crappie house with minnows and jigs. When the cools again the crappie should pick up. Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Bass are moving to deeper water ledges for the winter pattern.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish loaded up on brush piles in 12-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on the main lake brush 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using slow moving baits along banks with drop-offs. Crappie are good on minnows off docks. Sand bass are good with slabs mid lake chasing shad schools.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on laydowns in 10-18 feet of water up river.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass action remains strong with plenty of fish still being caught shallow, as water temperatures sit in the low 60s, though a noticeable trend of larger bass is developing deeper in the 15-25 foot range. Abundant grass remains throughout the lake, and baitfish are roaming in large schools, making forward-facing sonar an effective tool for targeting bass around shad. Largemouth bass up to 10.5 pounds were reported this week, along with solid numbers of 2-3 pound smallmouth bass. Holding in 35 feet or more, while crappie continue to relate to timber near drains, suspended in 5-20 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass can be caught in 5-10 feet near deep water on crankbaits. Crappie are in brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: The bass are fair with dropshots fished on the outside edge of healthier grass lines.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are suspended in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Slowly and steadily reel a white �¾ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye slabs off the bottom and anticipate that fish will follow. If your slab does not have a stinger hook, you are missing a lot of wintertime fish. Anticipate a majority of smaller fish in your catch, 9-12 inch white bass and undersized hybrid striped bass, with plenty of bonus largemouth bass and freshwater drum.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent with jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in the creek channels in 30-50 feet of water on timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with soft plastics. Crappie are slow on structure and roaming.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 65 degrees; Fishing remains slow overall, with limited action for redfish, stripers, and black bass, while catfish are also slow with only a few fish being caught from the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8 pounds are good in 3-18 feet of water on all around jigs in juice box, crankbaits on the rocks and docks, or on soft plastics scoping main lake pockets suspended over 18-25 feet. Crappie are excellent to 1.90 pounds on minnows, pink and yellow or shad colored jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles and docks in 18-22 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Stripers are good on live bait, or vertically jigging with half ounce to one ounce slab spoons. Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water on brush or timber piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and white bass have been on fire. being caught on a variety of things like rattle traps, underspin, Swimbaits, crank baits, spoons and Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass activity remains slow, and the lake is running about one foot below normal pool.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and smallmouth bass are good focusing on rocky drops and points.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: All boat ramps are currently closed, and anglers should contact Texas Parks and Wildlife for the most up-to-date access information; however, bank fishing remains very good, with catfish, black bass, crappie, and white bass being caught along the shoreline edges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass continue to be good in numbers on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are actively chasing shad along ledges, with deep-diving crankbaits performing well. Crappie continue to be productive on structure in 13-24 feet, with hair jigs producing best though plastics and minnows are also effective, as many bites have been very light. Hybrid stripers are being caught in good numbers in 17-33 feet on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad, with some fish coming on dead-sticking, a technique that will improve as water temperatures drop; anglers are also seeing many juvenile hybrids, so be sure to check identification guidelines through Texas Parks and Wildlife.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be slow in the river channels with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent roaming midlake to the dam with jigs, but have some minnows just in case. Black crappie are in 10-50 fish schools. White crappie are roaming solo in open water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Post front bass were biting small plastics ned rigs or shallow crankbaits.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are scattered with some good quality fish being caught. Dropshots are finally landing bass in 16-20 feet in the afternoon.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is slow, with a better bite midday to evening. Lake Fork crappie fishing is finally in a wintertime pattern. You can find large schools of crappie congregating on timber along creek channels in 35-60 feet of water. The winter bite on Lake Fork is the best time of year to catch a limit of crappie quickly and even catch some giant crappie mixed in with the eater size fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late on main lake points. Crappie are good in 16-18 feet deep in brush and on rock piles with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are also being caught at those deeper depths feeding on the bait fish. You might find bass on top where sand bass and striped bass are feeding. Crappie continue to be good suspended on timber and bridge pilings on many areas of the lake. Sand bass have been slow to fair on slabs and spinnerbaits near hoving birds mid-lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Deadsticking small slabs and small swimbaits on stinger hooks. Crappie and channel catfish are mixed in with the white bass.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are biting well on Texas-rigged worms and green Rage Craws around points, drop-offs, and cypress knees, and squarebill crankbaits in pilchard patterns diving 3-5 feet are producing along riprap. White bass action remains strong on the south end by trolling a 25-foot diver with a 3-foot leader and #12 Pet Spoon at 2.6-2.9 miles per hour in about 14 feet of water, with slabs and crankbaits also working near the West Fork.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with many smaller sized fish in soft plastics in brush piles. Crappie are on brush piles and roaming biting minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: A few bass caught on docks and brush with jigs and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very good on jigs or minnows. Crappie can be found in 30 feet of water suspended at 22-24 feet on trees. Bass have slowed down some but can still be found on structure in 10-15 feet of water. Jigs, crankbaits and jerkbaits fished in and over brush piles along the 10-15 feet on structure lines have taken the best bass. Crappie are stacking up on timber in the lower third of the lake off of the main channel.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-34 feet of water in brush piles, submerged timber, laydowns, bridge columns, and rock piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: More white bass, catfish and crappie are roaming fish in 18-24 feet of water. Crappie are on brush, roaming, and on the power line pylons biting minnows. Crappie eggs are still not fully developed yet. Largemouth bass are in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are being caught around creek channels, submerged timber, and points, with crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and soft plastics producing best, especially during warmer parts of the day. White bass and hybrid stripers are showing up in schools near deeper structure and along river channels, biting slabs, spoons, and live bait. Crappie are holding tight to brush and timber in deeper water, with minnows and jigs producing consistent bites for patient anglers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14 feet of water on remote brush piles with jigs or minnows. No reports of white bass or largemouth bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 9 pounds, with most fish 2-3 pounds. No reports on crappie this week.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush and roaming open water with jigs or minnows. Bass are slow with soft plastics in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on timber in 16-25 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Largemouth bass are good in the creeks with moving baits, or on docks with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in deep water on minnows. Black bass, sand bass and hybrids are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 18-21 feet. Bass moved to deep ledges.

reports.text: Black bass could still be caught on boat dock poles with a medium to shallow water crankbait and cover water.

reports.text: Bass are still heavily targeting bait balls and feeding up during this winter time.

reports.text: Crappie are good on concrete structure, docks and at the crappie house with any colored smaller profile jig. Bass are good with small squarebill crankbaits on rocky points in the cove near the crappie house.

reports.text: Slowly and steadily work white �¾ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs up off the bottom and anticipate that fish will follow produced well in deeper water. Anticipate a by-catch of outsized largemouth bass and freshwater drum when working these slabs deep under brighter conditions.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will continue to settle in on deeper structures in 20-30 feet of water with jigs and dead minnows being the bait of choice.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Unseasonably warm conditions at Toledo Bend have pushed water temperatures back into the upper 60s and low 70s, and bass fishing has been very good, with fish being caught from 2-25 feet of water on a wide variety of presentations. Shallow fish are responding well to squarebills, lipless crankbaits, and swim jigs, while deeper bass are being taken on crankbaits, Carolina rigs, and spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good targeting fish in 10-20 feet of water around drains and creek channels not far from the main lake with soft plastics and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on live minnows and jigs on brush.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good at the crappie house with minnows and jigs. When the cools again the crappie should pick up. Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Bass are moving to deeper water ledges for the winter pattern.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are holding on brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Fishing remains consistent but the crappie bite has slowed. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 18-25 feet of water in the channel and on timber off the main river channel and minor creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are suspended isolated in the main basin or in schools on deep trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 18-30 feet next to structures with live minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been slow, but picking up a few on chatterbaits and spinnerbaits around grass and bushes. Crappie are inconsistent. Crappie can be found from the 897 Bridge to the dam.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Redfish, catfish, black bass, and stripers are all seeing limited activity, with few consistent bites reported as conditions remain tough.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good on docks, offshore brush piles, and suspended above boulders with minnows and there is a decent bite jig bite in 8-15 feet and 25-45 feet. Largemouth bass bite is decent using deep crankbait, Alabama rigs, and swimbaits for deeper schooling fish, or on banks in the morning with crankbaits and chatterbaits on main lake rock and docks. White bass and hybrids are biting decently on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Stripers are good on live bait and vertically jigging with �½-1 ounce slab spoons. Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water on brush or timber piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: This water temperature will make it hard on these bass for a few days until they adjust to the colder water. Florida bass do not do well when the water drops fast, and they just will not bite.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Redfish, stripers, and black bass activity has been limited, with few consistent patterns developing.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth fishing has slowed down a bit.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing has been excellent, with good action reported for catfish, crappie, white bass, and black bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been fair, with most fish holding around standing timber and along extended points.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports from largemouth bass anglers boast 40 plus fish a day with an occasional bigger fish up to 7 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are performing well along offshore ledges and structure, often relating to large schools of shad with occasional schooling activity. Crappie have been productive around timber and structure in 13-28 feet, with hair jigs outperforming plastics and minnows, though many bites have been light. Hybrid striped bass are being caught in good numbers in 18-34 feet, both scattered and schooling, on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad, with many juveniles reported–be sure to check tooth patch for proper identification.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with some small bass catches trolling with deep diving crankbaits midlake and mid river. No reports or crappie.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are scattered with some good quality fish being caught.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite has slowed down after the cold fronts. A few bass can be caught in 5-7 feet of water on the flats with lipless crankbaits and suspending jerkbaits. Lake Fork crappie fishing is finally in a wintertime pattern. You can find large schools of crappie congregating on timber along creek channels in 35-60 feet of water. The winter bite on Lake Fork is the best time of year to catch a limit of crappie quickly and even catch some giant crappie mixed in with the eater size fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Quality crappie are feeding in deep structure biting jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 14-18 feet of water on brush and rock piles. Bass are slow with slow moving baits on main lake points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best reports continue to be crappie numbers fished around submerged structures. Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics near drop-offs near main lake points and near deeper docks. Some good black bass reports are coming from fishing laydowns in the river above Granbury.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Now is the time to start deadsticking small slabs and small swimbaits on stinger hooks. Some crappie and catfish are mixed in with the sandies.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are being found in drains within back lakes and along south-end drains where clearer water exists, with secondary points and docks holding fish when shallow areas are less productive; spinnerbaits, crankbaits, grubs, and Texas-rigged worms have all been effective. White bass fishing remains excellent, especially on the south end where larger fish are concentrated, with paddle-tail soft plastics, trolling a No.12 Pet Spoon behind a Jet Diver, and vertical jigging slabs producing steady action once schools are located. Catfish are fair on punch bait or fresh shad fished on the bottom in 8-15 feet of water near main river channels, while crappie are being caught in 10-15 feet…
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow, but can be caught on brush in 10-15 feet with Alabama rigs, small paddle tail swimbaits, and small minnow type baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are related to bait and the bait has slid out to the mid depth up to 25 feet over major structure changes. The bass bite has been a little slow in the mornings but picking up in the afternoon. Shad color crankbaits are working, and it may be time to pull out the Alabama rig and go after the bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very good on jigs or minnows. Crappie can be found in 30 feet of water suspended at 22-24 feet on trees. Bass have slowed down some but can still be found on structure in 10-15 feet of water. Jigs, crankbaits and jerkbaits fished in and over brush piles along the 10-15 feet on structure lines have taken the best bass. Crappie are in a full winter pattern with fish moving to deeper timber and roaming open water near the dam. Crappie are good with two inch plastics with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are deep hugging the bottom of humps, in 25-30 feet on structure, and hugging silt bottoms. Some crappie can be caught in 6-12 feet in the private boat slips with structure from 7-9 a.m. then from 3 p.m. to dark. Small swimbaits on 5/8 ounce jigheads, minnows, or slabs will work. Expect to catch crappie, catfish, or a largemouth while targeting sandies. Black bass are in 15-20 feet of water on laydowns and rock piles. Any super sharp drop-offs in 15 feet of water are producing bass with Carolina rigged jigs or a 5/8 ounce jig with a jerkbait soft plastic minnow attached free swimming it over the bass if you have live scope.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush, roaming, and on the power line pylons. Crappie eggs are still not fully developed yet. Largemouth bass are in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are scattered relating to points, submerged timber, and offshore structure, with slower presentations producing best results. White bass and hybrid stripers are mixed between deeper water and schooling activity when bait is present, while crappie are being found around brush and timber in deeper water but can be finicky.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the hydrilla with light colored swimbaits, chrome rattle traps and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are fair to good around brush piles in 10-15 feet of water using tube jigs and minnows. Sand bass are good with slab spoons around the warm water discharge.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow with a Colorado blade spinnerbait or a shallow diving crankbait on main lake points. Crappie are excellent on chartreuse and black crappie jigs on a split shot rig or live minnows. Crappie are deep and suspended on timber, so it is best to timber hop with live-scope. Catfish are excellent with live minnows, or a crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs or deep diving crankbaits offshore in 18-22 feet of water. Crappie are good with chartreuse and black crappie jigs, the lighter weight the better.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations are strong, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are good on swimbaits and jigs along grass edges. Crappie are slow in 8 feet of water with white crappie jigs, the lighter the weight the better.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. No reports of white bass or largemouth bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass fair to 5 pounds with underspins, swimbaits, finesse jigs and green pumpkin, or Alabama rig with 3.25 inch swimbaits in 8-18 feet of water. The upper end of the lake is slow for bass. Crappie are slow with few reports around deeper trees on river channels ledges around Bull Hollow and Elm Creek.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Unless we get several days of sub-freezing temperatures in January or early February, the season is being set for an early crappie spawn and a great bass spawn. Crappie bite should be in the shallows by mid-January pending there is not a freeze. Bass anglers should start looking at the northern early spawning areas, Flat, Neches River, and Kickapoo Creek now for signs of pre-spawn and staging.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids, sand bass, and black bass are slow. Crappie are biting in deep water on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with swimbaits and jigs along grass lines. Crappie are good on deep brush piles with white and clear crappie jigs, the lighter the weight the better.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish in those areas with two or three jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair as fish move out from brush to the deeper water along flats and levees.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on main lake brush piles 35-45 feet of water, and in the creeks in 12-18 feet of water on timber and in deep holes. Crappie are good with natural colored jigs or minnows. Sand bass are fair on humps with live bait, or slabs. Largemouth bass are fair to good running in pockets, ditches and draws with a swim jig. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Fish can be caught on slabs and spinnerbaits in 18-25 feet. Black bass will be using the hard cover as the water temperature declines. Alabama rigs can be a great option if you have a livescope to target bass on standing timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows holding tight beneath brush in 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and slow plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: It is necessary to slow down with �¾ ounce white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab. Largemouth bass are beginning to move into deep timber where the same slab is effective in drawing strikes while the slab is being drilled upward, or while snap jig near bottom.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is steady. The largemouth bite is surprisingly good right now.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: No crappie reports at this time.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass love the water temperature and fish 3-4 pounds are possible. Bass are 30-40 feet down on the main lake bluff walls biting big imitation shad baits. Bass are very active and chasing baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows or jigs in old creek beds, grouping up in 20-30 feet of water or in brush piles in 16 feet. Bass are fair with bigger fish being caught on spinnerbaits or trick worms scattered in 6-10 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Fishing remains consistent but the crappie bite has slowed. Crappie are fair on main lake brush 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but a few are caught on slow moving baits. Crappie are good under the bridge. Sand bass good bouncing slabs off bottom in mid lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough while fish are transitioning to deeper water. Crappie are suspended isolated in the main basin or in schools on deep trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad and bluegill gearing up for winter. Use live-scop to locate offshore bass and have an umbrella rig or a minnow on a jig head ready. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: There is a good shallow bass bite early, but quickly slows down after the sun is up. Bass are biting hard and soft jerkbaits around the edges of submerged grass, with mid-strolling minnow-style plastics producing on nomadic open-water fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Change to a slower presentation using Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-30 feet next to timber with live minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in timber from 20-40 feet of water with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good mid morning to the afternoon in 5-8 feet of water suspending jerkbaits around pond dams and bushes. Crappie are excellent on tree tops in river channels with minnows on a 1/16 ounce jighead. Crappie can be found from the 897 Bridge to the dam.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Black bass continue to be slow as well, with most anglers working hard for just a handful of strikes throughout the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 8-15 feet of water on docks, and in 25-45 feet of water on offshore brush piles with minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass are fair using deep crankbaits and swimbaits for deeper schooling fish or on banks in the morning with crankbaits and chatterbaits on main lake rock and docks. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.84 pounds are good in 3-18 feet of water on bladed jigs, crankbaits and jigs. Crappie are good to 10 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 12-18 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Vertical jigging has produced the best action with �½-1 ounce slab spoons. Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water on brush or timber piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Catching the bass on Alabama rigs, shad pattern rattle traps, white chatterbaits, big swimbaits, or flukes. Look for bait balls in the river or bayou systems to find white bass and black bass running.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Redfish remain slow in 5-10 feet, and both black bass and stripers are also sluggish, showing limited activity despite mild conditions.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass are in a fall transition.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good stacks of hybrid striped bass and white bass are being found on mid-lake points and drop-offs along sandy flats throughout the entire lake including the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch, and the spillway humps in 8-14 feet of water. Cast spinnerbaits and slabs, and watch for schooling fish on these flats as well as around deeper seawalls and shorelines. Target hybrids with a spinnerbait or work a slab vertically with a fast up-and-down motion. A slow retrieve with a slab cast and reeled steadily back is also effective. Try rattle traps, spoons, umbrella rigs, slabs, or sassy shads to trigger bites. The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Some black bass, crappie, and white bass are also being picked up from the bank, though in smaller numbers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow, with most bites coming from timber in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast limits of largemouth bass to 8 pounds and eater sized channel catfish. Largemouth are good on soft plastics worked near points and creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are active on offshore structure and along shad-filled banks, with deep crankbaits on ledges and Texas-rigged plastics or creature baits working best early and late. Crappie numbers remain strong around timber and structure in 13-28 feet, hitting hair jigs, plastics, and minnows, though bites have been light. Hybrid action is solid, with fish scattered and schooling in 18-34 feet, taking slabs, spoons, larger minnows, and shad; many juveniles are showing up, so check tooth patches for proper ID.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: The pattern remains the same but in the coming week expect crappie to pull off structure and roam. Lots of small crappie are on timber and brush. Keeper crappie are coming off the bridge columns with minnows. Open water suspending crappie are easily spooked due to continuous boat traffic.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow with some small bass catches trolling with deep diving crankbaits midlake and mid river. No reports or crappie or catfish.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow pitching Texas rigs in 6 feet of water against the trees. The morning bass bite continues in shallow water with rattletraps and underspins.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is best over flats and long points with chatterbaits, spinnerbaits and lipless crankbaits in 5-7 feet. Black bass are feeding in the backs of creeks and coves. Cooler nights have dropped water temperatures and bass are cruising the shallows. Streamers are enticing bass early and late in the day. Lake Fork crappie fishing is about as hot as it has ever been going into the last week of November. Fast limits of crappie can be caught off all kinds of structure. The lake has tons of keeper sized black crappie congregated on brush piles, tire reefs, underwater bridges, regular bridges, road beds, humps, points, ledges and timber. Lots of big white crappie are on deeper…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with the best bite on slow moving baits. Crappie are good on minnows in 14-18 feet on deep brush or rock piles. The bite is good on slabs and buck tail jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow to fair on slabs and small jigs worked in 20 feet of water near channel ledges from Decordova to Ports O-Call. Crappie action continues to be good on small jigs worked near submerged structures like timber and bridge pilings. Black bass action is good to 6 pounds on soft plastics worked near main lake points and in the back of sloughs on those warmer afternoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in a full winter pattern holding on deeper docks, points, and any pockets of slightly clearer water around spots like the golf course waterfall, the south end, and protected points. Crappie have slowed due to muddy conditions, though the East Fork should clear first and pick up sooner.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Cooler weather has bass holding shallow and relating to visible cover.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with a big worm on a Texas rig targeting structure and brush, or with a wacky worm around docks and against the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough while fish are transitioning to deeper water. Crappie are suspended isolated in the main basin or in schools on deep trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is very good this week. Crappie are biting extremely well on live minnows and a wide range of jigs, with fish responding to almost any well-presented offering. Largemouth bass fishing was good over the weekend, with quality better than numbers. Additional bass were taken on deep-diving suspended jerkbaits worked over the tops of brush piles. Crappie are in a full winter pattern with fish moving to deeper timber and roaming open water near the dam. Crappie are good with two inch plastics with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: After the cold snap crappie are deep hugging the bottom of humps, in 25-30 feet on structure, and hugging silt bottoms. Some crappie can be caught in 6-12 feet in the private boat slips with structure from 7-9 a.m. then from 3 p.m. to dark. Small swimbaits on 5/8 ounce jigheads, minnows, or slabs will work. Expect to catch crappie, catfish, or a largemouth while targeting sandies. Black bass are in 15-20 feet of water on laydowns and rock piles. Any super sharp drop-offs in 15 feet of water are producing bass with Carolina rigged jigs or a 5/8 ounce jig with a jerkbait soft plastic minnow attached free swimming it over the bass if you have live scope.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25 feet of water on brush piles with minnows or jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Look for bass suspended around grass or isolated structure and throw an Alabama rig, underspin or minnow.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-34 feet of water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Target largemouth bass in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs. Crappie are will scatter on cloudy cold days and bunch up on warm sunny days. Some crappie will also start suspending on timber and in the middle of creek channels. Some crappie have eggs already.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are offering opportunity–largemouths have been active on deeper points using Carolina-rigged worms, spinners, or jigs. Crappie are producing around structure and creek mouths with jigs or minnows when the water’s a bit clearer. White bass are still a possibility on spoons and slabs, particularly near humps or main-lake structure early and late.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on most of the lake. Fishing the hydrilla is always good while bass are moving into the creeks. Crappie are scattered, but also moving towards warmer waters. Sand bass are good from the Dirgin bridge to the warm water outlet using slab spoons and tail spinners bouncing off the bottom.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with chartreuse and black squarebill crankbaits or bluegill bladed jigs holding tight to rocky main lake points. Crappie are excellent on chartreuse and black crappie jigs on a split shot rig. Crappie are deep and suspended on timber, so it is best to timber hop with live-scope. Catfish are excellent with live minnows, or a crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on Carolina rigs or deep diving crankbaits offshore in 15-22 feet of water. Crappie are good with chartreuse and black crappie jigs, the lighter weight the better.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations are strong, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are good offshore in 15-22 feet of water on Carolina jigs, or deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are fair in 8 feet of water with white crappie jigs, the lighter the weight the better.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Primarily undersized fish with some limits of good sized crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good for catches up to 5 pounds. Bass are in 8-18 feet of water hitting small minnow baits on underspins. Shake the minnows around schools of bass chasing suspended shad. Crappie are slow but reports of some still being caught on main lake deep trees along the river channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair in 12 feet of water on flukes and Carolina rigged craw baits. Crappie are good on deep brush piles with white and chartreuse crappie jigs, the lighter the weight the better.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Silver and white slab jigs have been the magic ticket. The largemouth bass winter pattern is starting. Bass are feeding on the shad around docks and structure. Bass are eating, but not in a hurry. Sand bass are good in 25-35 feet of water on main lake points and sand flats with slabs.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in 18-21 feet. Bass have moved to deep ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair and also moving out from brush and in the deeper water along flats and levees.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have moved to main lake brush piles 35-40 feet of water. Crappie are good with natural colored jigs or minnows. Sand bass are fair on humps with live bait, or slabs. Largemouth bass are fair to good running in pockets, ditches and draws with a swim jig. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Fish can be caught deadsticking flukes or hitting slabs, and Pet Spoons. The colder the water gets the more the black bass will get on hard structures near drop-offs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows holding tight under brush in 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and slow plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent on concrete structure, docks and at the crappie house with any colored smaller profile jig. When crappie quit biting on the dock or in the crappie house, that is typically a sign that bass are in the area. Bass are good with small squarebill crankbaits on rocky points in the cove near the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Change to a slower presentation using Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs. As a bonus, quality largemouth bass are now showing up in big numbers in deep water, especially where timber exists. This same Slab will remain effective in catching these fish through February. Bass activity has improved, with many fish chasing shad in open water.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing will continue to improve as the water temperatures have fallen into the mid 50s and the crappie start to settle in on structure and brush piles in 20-30 feet of water. Bass are starting to settle into a winter pattern. Look to find bass feeding and hanging on shallow structures and flats on sunny days, and hanging a little deeper off the banks on main lake points and structures on cloudy days. Stripers are good on the ledges and in deeper water with slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing continues to improve as the weather becomes colder. Bass love the water temperature and fish 3-4 pounds are possible. Bass are 30-40 feet down on the main lake bluff walls biting big imitation shad baits. Bass are very active and chasing baits. A variety of techniques are producing bass across the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good in deeper water brush piles with live minnows.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and difficult to find. Crappie may be transitioning to deep channels and ledges. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are slow with fish suspending in the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Run the main channels in deeper water looking for crappie in open water and looking at structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on main lake brush 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing fair using baits with slow presentation. Crappie are slow. Sand bass are good on slabs bounced off the bottom near schools of shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a full winter pattern with fish moving to deeper timber and roaming open water near the dam. Crappie are fair on two inch plastics with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30-45 feet over brush with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has also been good, with fish holding in sunken brush in 5-15 feet of water and hitting ⅛-ounce jig heads paired with small baitfish-style plastics. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 20-25 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Bass are good on spinnerbaits in 5-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Game fish like largemouth bass and sand bass will be around the balls of shad in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie are beginning to suspend across the basin for winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad and bluegill gearing up for winter. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting jerkbaits worked along the edge of submerged vegetation.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: When the water temperature hits 60 degrees, we will be switching over to the 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in timber from 20-40 feet of water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Starting to see groups of bass staging offshore in 10-17 feet around pond dams and high spots. Crappie are schooling up, but the fish are not very active so the bite is slow. Some reports of crappie in the creeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 66 degrees; Catfish, stripers, and black bass are running slow this week, but redfish remain solid in front of the power plant, with most fish weighing 5-10 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on docks, and offshore brush piles in 8-15 feet of water or 25-35 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Largemouth bass are fair using deep crankbaits and swimbaits for deeper schooling fish, or along banks, main lake rock and docks in the morning with crankbaits and chatterbaits. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8 pounds are good in 13-28 feet of water on Alabama rigs and scope minnows, or along the shoreline on bladed jigs, crankbaits and jigs in 3-8 feet of water. Crappie are excellent to 12 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 10-15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to school up and bite in the main lake. Shad pattern baits are the way to go for black bass and the white bass.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers are slow this week, but bank fishing overall continues to produce solid action for those soaking baits and covering shoreline structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good stacks of hybrid striped bass and white bass are being found on mid-lake points and drop-offs along sandy flats throughout the entire lake including the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch, and the spillway humps in 8-14 feet of water. Cast spinnerbaits and slabs, and watch for schooling fish on these flats as well as around deeper seawalls and shorelines. To target hybrids use spinnerbaits or work a slab vertically with a fast up-and-down motion. A slow retrieve with a slab cast and reeled steadily back is also effective. Try rattle traps, spoons, umbrella rigs, slabs, or sassy shads to trigger bites. The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good, while crappie are running slow. Black bass are producing decent action but only from the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been slow, with most fish holding around timber in 5-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: This attracts many bass anglers from all over in the winter. Fishing is excellent with most folks reporting numbers of largemouth being caught with an occasional bigger fish to 8 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush in 10-25 feet on minnows and jigs, with numbers improving, though many are undersized and fishing pressure is increasing as word gets out. Largemouth bass have been active along edges and schooling on shad, with crankbaits and creature baits producing well. Hybrid striped bass remains scattered but schooling at times, with fish found on flats in 16-34 feet using slabs, spoons, or shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Lots of small crappie are on timber and brush. Keeper crappie are coming off the bridge columns with minnows. Expect crappie to pull off structure within the next two weeks. Open water suspending crappie are easily spooked due to continuous boat traffic.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow on spinnerbaits and wacky worms in the early morning. Crappie are slow with minnows.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers
