reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows around boat docks and pushing shallow due to water temperature. Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and jerkbaits. White bass are fair on slabs over humps and points Perch are good on nightcrawlers around docks.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing, however, is improving, with fish holding on isolated man-made brush piles and vertical standing timber on flats along the river channel and at the mouths of creeks leading into spawning areas.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite has slowed but is fair with chatterbaits around clumps of grass or lipless crankbaits in the flats. Black Bass are feeding in the backs of creeks and coves. Cooler nights have dropped water temperatures and bass are cruising the shallows. Streamers are enticing bass early and late in the day. Lake Fork crappie fishing is about as hot as it has ever been going into the last week of November. Fast limits of crappie can be caught off all kinds of structure. The lake has tons of keeper sized black crappie congregated on brush piles, tire reefs, underwater bridges, regular bridges, road beds, humps, points, ledges and timber. Lots of big white crappie are on deeper timber…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving deeper as the water temp drops. Crappie are in 18-20 feet of water on structure with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 14 feet of water with minnows. Bass are slow due to the cold water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass continue to be fair to good for fish up to 5 pounds. Sand bass and small stripers are fair to good on slabs and spinnerbaits fished on flats near Ports-O-Call and near Indian Harbor. Crappie action continues to be good on the main lake on submerged structure using small minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Now is the time to start deadsticking small slabs and small swimbaits. Crappie and catfish are mixed in with the sandies.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are moving shallow with the warming water and biting spinnerbaits, topwaters, crankbaits, twitch baits, grubs, and Texas-rigged plastics in green or dark colors. Crappie are tight to structure in main channels and overlooked areas, hitting minnows and hand-tied jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting around shallow cover and structure following the recent refill after drawdown.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough, but bass can be caught.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Game fish like largemouth bass and sand bass will be around the balls of shad in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie are beginning to suspend across the basin for winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish holding in timber from Watts Island up to Alley Creek. Recent rains and cooler temperatures have pushed bass into deeper water. Bass are good on black-and-blue jigs and Alabama rigs fished around structure in 11–15 feet. Crappie are sitting on flats off the main channel in 6-20 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Switch to red chatterbaits, red rattle traps, and Texas to catch largemouth bass in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks. Crappie are will scatter on cloudy cold days and bunch up on warm sunny days. Some crappie will also start suspending on timber and in the middle of creek channels. Some crappie have eggs already.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are active, especially around submerged timber and rocky points, with shallow water producing well early and late in the day. Crappie are scattered around brush piles and standing timber in 10-20 feet of water, biting on minnows and small jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on most of the lake. Fishing the hydrilla is always good with bass moving into the creek’s. Crappie are scattered more but also moving towards warmer waters. Sand bass are good from the Dirgin bridge to the warm water outlet using slab spoons and tail spinners bouncing off the bottom.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass and sand bass are great and continue to flourish around many parts of the lake. Crappie are slow from Sanford Yake Dock, North Canyon, and Fritch Fortress with pearl white, pearl blue, grey or yellow jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with flat sided crankbaits and squarebill crankbaits shallow around rocky points. Crappie are fair on standing timber mid lake with a 1/32 ounce white and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Carolina rigs or medium diving crankbaits on creek channel beds on the south side of the lake. Crappie are fair with 1/32 ounce black and chartreuse crappie jigs in timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations are strong, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are fair on flukes with a light weight. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass are heavily related to baitfish this time of year, so a good rule of thumb is find the bait and then you will find the bass. Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-5 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sunlight. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Baitfish are in the backs of pockets and upriver with the bass close behind. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass numbers are good with catches up to 8 pounds. No reports for crappie. Catches up to 2.5 pounds are being reported on slabs and jigging spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will start to transition into the creeks. Crappie are good in 16-25 feet of water with jigs or minnows. Bass and hybrids should be more open water oriented chasing bait balls.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were biting in deep water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on flukes and topwater around grassy points. Crappie are good with schools in deep trees on jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 18-21 feet. Bass are moved to deep ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and in brush piles in 18-25 feet of water, and on bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on slabs and spinnerbaits. As the temperature cools the black bass will seek hard cover, such as rock, stumps, and dock poles. Bass can still be shallow, but will use the hard cover. Bass can be caught on jigs, squarebill crankbaits, and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: The creeks and upriver areas have turned a bit muddy, but bass are moving shallow to chase shad in the new water. Spinnerbaits and traps are producing well when covering water and targeting feeding fish, and any remaining grass is holding bass. Crankbaits and swim jigs are good for covering ground, while crappie and white bass are also trending upriver. The major populations of bass are in 10-15 feet of water or 20-25 feet of water on main lake drains, or secondary points and creek channel swings.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair using crankbaits and spinnerbaits on rocks from the shore to three feet, with the occasional deeper catch. Crappie are good to excellent with pink and white or black and chartreuse jigs in 9-11 feet of water on brush or concrete structures. Some crappie can be caught in the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: When the water temperature hits 60 degrees, we will be switching over to the 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab. Bass are being caught from nomadic schools following shad in open water, best located with forward-facing sonar. Football jigs are also catching bass around rocky structures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits and slabs are working best, however, be looking for these fish to move offshore and into deeper water soon. Crappie fishing is better this week than weeks previous. Largemouth are very good with squarebill crankbaits in super shallow water next to dock legs and shallow stickups.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Look for bass in coves with brush and structure. Bass should start to chase big gizzard shad. Still seeing a lot of undersized crappie this fall. Stripers are good under the birds or ledges and drop-offs in 10-30 feet of water with slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures have dropped back into the low 60s and upper 50s, and although the lake didn’t receive as much rain as expected, bass fishing remains strong. For deeper bass in 22-28 feet, Carolina rigs, drop shots, and spoons are producing the most consistent action.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair using a variety of techniques, though main lake areas have been the most productive.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows or jigs in old creek beds, grouping up in 20-25 feet of water or brush piles in 16 feet. Bass are fair on spinnerbaits, trick worms and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will be slower after the cold front. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are good on brush piles with minnows and jigs. A few crappie are showing up in the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: As the water temperature drops expect crappie to move to deeper brush and use minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on main lake brush 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with a few catches using slow bait presentations. Crappie are slow. Sand bass are good bouncing jigs and slabs off bottom near schools of shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on deeper timber and brush. You can also find crappie roaming and suspended.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-35 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 5-10 feet of water in grass with Texas rig worms, wacky rigged senkos and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been decent lately on Lake Austin.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the weeds on plastic worms or jig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be slow, try offshore brush piles or deep water in front of main lake docks. Check way up in the backs of coves for Largemouth Bass, find the bait, find the fish.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.20 pounds are slow on Hag’s Tsunami half ounce jigs in Juice Box and crankbaits in 2-6 feet. Bass are settling into a normal winter pattern. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 12-15 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish feeding up.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on red rattle traps, green pumpkin trick worms on the shaky head, or a white color spinnerbait in 2-6 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: The fish are biting good with mostly catches of bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek power plant lake continues to produce numbers of largemouth bass on soft plastics fished near creek channels and main lake points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good shallow and deep with bigger fish offshore on structure with jerkbait and swimbaits. Crappie are in 13-22 feet of water close or in structure, and timber with jigs and minnows. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs and jigging.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Largenouith bass are staging at the end of points and creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Cooler water so the bass will be deeper. Black bass are slow in 5-10 feet. Some smaller bass are chasing shad on warm days. Focus on creek bends and drop-offs. small streamers and top water patterns might catch active bass in creeks on warm days. The Lake Fork crappie fishing continues to be excellent as the surface temperatures continue to drop. If you find areas with tons of shad there will be crappie close by. Minnows are always a go to bait for crappie on Lake Fork.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is improving as the water clarity clears. Crappie are biting on minnows and jigs in about 15 feet of water near brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action is good to excellent near the bridge and in the river near Tin Top. Largemouth bass fishing is fair to good on soft plastics and lipless crankbaits worked near creek entrances and near laydowns on the upper ends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Use a deadstick technique with slabs on a stinger hook keeping the bait in the strike zone. Some crappie can randomly be mixed in.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with small bass eating Texas rig soft plastics. Crappie are holding on deep timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows in 12-16 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good working docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and flukes. Largemouth bass are good on red rattle traps, green pumpkin trick worms on the shaky head, or a white color spinnerbait in 2-6 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but should improve once the lake stabilizes after rain. Tilapia beds will produce good bass when you find them using dropshot worms and Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow in 25 feet over standing timber with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being seen in deeper water in larger groups. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits, Carolina rigs and dropshots. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and standing timber with a 1/16 ounce white crappie jig on a split shot.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good out in the lake. Crappie are sucking it in and swimming away versus hitting it hard. A 7.76 pound largemouth bass caught off the dock with a minnow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair to 7 pounds on the main lake with crankbaits, shaky heads and swimbaits. Crappie are fair on main lake deep trees 25-40 feet of water. Crappie seem to be suspended 15-20 feet in the brush tops.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: What we are looking forward to, though is warmer than average temperatures, at least so far into this winter, could lead to earlier movement of white bass up the creeks, and earlier movement of both bass and crappie into the shallower nesting and spawning areas of the lake, particularly in the northern part if we do not get heavy rainfall.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to bite on minnows and jigs. Hybrids, black bass, and sand bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 30-38 feet of water and use a �¾ ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 18-28 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass fishing can be rated fair with a few catches being made with a slab and jig combination fished on the bottom in 25-30 feet of water off main lake points and Pelican Island. Hybrid striper action is fair on live bait and slabs off main lake points, Pelican Island and Windsock Point in 30 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are moving shallow into the bush with the new water. Bass are on the move upriver in shallow water with crankbaits and swim jigs. Crappie and white bass are going up river.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnow over brush 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are slow on slow moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Use your electronics to locate active crappie on brush and structure near coves and points in 18-25 feet of water. For bass fishing, look for fish moving off points to secondary ledges and humps. On sunny days, target rocky coves, as bass will pull up to feed in the warmer shallows.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: There is a new moon coming this week which should get the female bass thinking about getting ready to make a move up. No reports on crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing shad in the backs of coves and cuts near deeper water. Largemouth bass are good on red rattle traps, green pumpkin trick worms on the shaky head, or a white color spinnerbait in 2-6 feet of water. In the river crawfish colored crankbaits are landing bass on bluff walls and points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 20-25 feet of water. Bass are slow on crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the Crappie House on jigs and minnows. Bass and catfish are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been good using a variety approaches. Bass are good with catches up to 5 pounds, and some Guadalupe bass up to 2 pounds. Grass was holding most of the bass. The bigger bass are coming in 6-12 feet but there are plenty of bass up against the shores.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working worms and flukes around any water vegetation have been the most productive. The outlet will always produce some bass too. Bass are good with deep points and humps holding a few better size fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Windy, sunny banks and retaining walls are good bets for black bass. On warm, sunny days, small shad pattern flies might produce bass around submerged vegetation.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is excellent in the main river channel timber and lower third of the lake in 30-50 feet of water catching crappie 6-28 feet down. Fish are very healthy with big black crappie being caught on jigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught in weeds on plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.40 pounds are good on 1/8 ounce minnow baits scoping and Hag’s Tsunami 1/2 ounce jigs in Juice Box in 1-5 feet of water along weed edges, and Alabama rigs on the ledges. Bass are settling into a normal winter pattern. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 12-15 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Crappie seem to be in the river channels. White bass, yellow bass and crappie are biting decent even with the black bass.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good along grass edges with rattle traps, watermelon red senkos, just off the grass in 14 feet of water cast an Alabama rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good shallow and deep with bigger fish on offshore structure with jerkbaits and swimbaits. Crappie are in 13-22 feet close or in structure using jigs and minnows. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them and get ready for deadsticking.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and difficult to pattern due to fluctuating weather. Some bass can be caught with Carolina rigs, shaky heads, or rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Offshore look for the bass to be on road beds and high spots in 15-22 feet with Carolina rigs and spoons. The Lake Fork crappie fishing continues to be excellent as the surface temperatures continue to drop. If you find areas with tons of shad there will be crappie close by. Minnows are always a go to bait for crappie on Lake Fork.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are improving in 15 feet of water on brush with jigs and minnows. Bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are under the birds or search with a graph using the deadstick technique with slabs on a stinger hook.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow on spinnerbaits along the bank, and with soft plastics from the bank to 25 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 20-30 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie are hugging the bottom so you have to let a ⅛ ounce hand tied jig touch the bottom and then slowly lift to entice a bite. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been getting them. Expect to catch a couple black bass in your journey to the blackwater. Black bass are in 1-5 feet on rocks or concrete with Texas rigs, or in 15-20 feet on brush piles with jigs. The dam has trees and brush bluegill and crappie are mixed in. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows in 12-16 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good working docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and flukes. In the Colorado arm bass are biting Alabama rigs and jerkbaits, or under docks with green pumpkin senkos.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 6-38 feet of water. Bass are scattered from 6-20 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fattening up for the spawn in a couple months. Crappie are in 10-18 feet on offshore brush with minnows, or tight lining straight down in standing timber. Largemouth bass can be caught from 2-18 feet this week on docks, timber, bulkheads, rocks with Texas rigs, jigs, chatterbaits, and spinnerbait. Numbers of bass are still on offshore brush and roaming main lake points.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in pre-spawn to spawn depending on the area of the lake. Crappie are a bit slow but should pick up when water temperatures stabilize better.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with some catches to 12 pounds with shad patterned swimbaits or crankbaits. Crappie seem to be good on deep trees in river bends in 25-30 feet suspended in tops of trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass will have breif feeding periods in December and January until they feel the beginnings of the spawn stage, so slower, larger baits with some vibration could be more effective. Crappie should remain deep during the winter.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass fishing fair to good using a slab and jig combination fished on the bottom in 25-30 feet of water off main lake points and near Pelican Island. Hybrid striper action is fair on live bait and slabs off main lake points and Windsock Point in 30 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing shad in the shallows and off points. When you can find grass on the south end there is usually a bass that can be caught on crankbaits. Crappie and white bass are moving in the river channel, but are not stacked up in the river like normal.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has slowed down but can still be rewarding for patient anglers. Crappie are holding tight to brush piles in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing shad in the backs of coves and cuts near deeper water. Bass are good around grass and hydrilla midlake to the dam with red chatterbaits, or shad colored hybrid hunter. In the river crawfish colored crankbaits are landing bass on bluff walls and points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. White bass fishing is slow but some are being caught up the river on flukes and slabs. Largemouth bass are good around the docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-30 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been good using a variety approaches.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working worms and flukes around any water vegetation have been the most productive. The outlet will always produce some bass too. Bass are hiding in the edge of the reeds and what little grass there is holding bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in the early mornings, but the midday bite has been the best with Texas rigs and Viper XP Jigs on big timber around fence rows and creeks and ditches are best in 4-8 feet. Crappie fishing is excellent in the main river channel timber and lower third of the lake in 30-50 feet of water catching crappie 6-28 feet down. Fish are very healthy with big black crappie being caught on jigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and hybrids remain scattered, slabs and deadsticking main lake structure may bring a fish or two. Largemouth bass have been slow but shallow running crankbaits fished near main lake points are catching a few fish. Crappie remain sluggish in the stained water, a few fish are coming in on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.64 pounds are fair on 1/8 ounce minnow baits scoping and Hag’s Tsunami �½ ounce jigs in Juice Box in 1-5 feet along weed edges and on the ledges. Crappie are slow with fish up to 10 inches on white or black/chartreuse jigs and minnows in brush piles 10-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The white bass and black bass are running up the river pretty good chasing shad, look for the bait on your graph or pay attention to the birds on the lane poles. Alabama rigs, rattle traps, chatterbait, underspin or swimbait will work well for the black bass. and a rooster tail works good for the white bass. I am seeing my crappie friends showing up more and more so I would assume they are biting also.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite has been getting better. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 7-15 feet under bridge pylons, hidden brush piles throughout the lake or under docks. Crappie fisherman have been moving spot to spot finding limits. Lots of crappies in the 7-9 inch range. Limits of crappie will happen but you may catch a lot of small ones getting to your limit.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Number of largemouth bass on points and near creek channel ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good on shallow to offshore structure or schooling on shad. Crappie are in 12-22 feet close or in structure hitting jigs and minnows. Many anglers are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, slabs, or casting swimbaits or crankbaits when schooled up.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rattle traps and topwaters, shaky heads, and some dropshots in 2-20 feet of waters.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on Viper XP jigs and Texas rigs around big wood near any depth changes like creeks and ditches in 5-7 feet. Black bass are slow in 5-10 feet of water with Clousers with a sinking tip line are your best bet. Small streamers and top water patterns might catch active bass in creeks on warm days. You can find big numbers of black crappie at the base of shallow trees in 12-18 feet in the mid lake areas. Sometimes you will find white crappie in the same trees suspended halfway down. The black crappie are higher on the trees off shore and the white crappie are further down on the trees. We have seen some bigger crappie in the 2.5 pound range being caught so the winter time big fish…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair as anglers continue to wait for crappie to move to winter patterns on deep structures. Bass are slow with a shallow crankbait or spinnerbait on rocky structure on the south side.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush piles in about 15 feet of water. Bass are shallow on rocky banks good on crank baits and spinner baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Granbury sand bass and crappie are good on small jigs on the upper ends from in town to Tin Top. Largemouth bass are also good on soft plastics on the upper ends near points and laydowns. Some good largemouth are also being caught near major creek entrances near Decordova subdivision.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are on docks and structure eating just about anything as well. Crappie are deep and very tight to structure on the bottom being caught with minnows and small jigs but need to be enticed to bite a bit.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with some fish suspended on swim baits and Alabama rigs, and soft plastics in brush and near the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 20-30 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie need a bigger profile bait to zone in on. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been getting them. Expect to catch a couple black bass in your journey to the Blackwater. Black bass are still strong on white and chartreuse spinnerbaits with a half of a zoom motor oil worm as the trailer in 1-5 feet on rocks or concrete. Texas rig and bass jigs are pulling them out of 15-20 feet deep brush piles. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows in 12-16 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good working docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and flukes.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 6-38 feet of water. Bass are slow, with the best bite in the late morning slowly dragging soft plastics on a Texas rig or Ned rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Look for bass in deeper water as their food source has migrated deeper. Crappie have picked up fishing deep brush piles in 25-30 feet with shad colored jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with catches up to 11 pounds possible on large swimbaits and Carolina rigs off the bottom in creek channel swings in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are excellent in 12-15 feet of water and standing timber and brush piles with 1/16 ounce translucent white crappie jigs on a split shot rig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: There are still some large groups of bass in deeper water hovering just off the bottom, so a drop-shot has been working pretty well. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits, Carolina rigs and dropshots. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and standing timber with a 1/16 ounce white crappie jig on a split shot.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with reports of one 10 pound fish and a few more to 7 pounds. Crappie are slow on deeper trees in The Colorado River bends in 15-25 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass will have brief feeding periods in December and January until they feel the beginnings of the spawn stage, so slower, larger baits with some vibration could be more effective. Crappie should remain deep during the winter.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent for numbers with many fish in the 3-5 pound range. Crappie are good on small white jigs on a split shot rig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass are moving up with the lake level rising. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 30-38 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 18-28 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass fishing has improved and can be rated good with reports of catches being made on slabs fished on the bottom in 25-30 feet of water off Pelican Island, main lake points and the 309 Flats. Hybrid striper action is fair on live bait and slabs off main lake points and Windsock Point in 30 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good trending towards excellent fishing concrete submerged structures. The crappie house is starting to draw more anglers. Crappie have a belly full of shad. Bass are fair casting a small squarebill crankbait along shallow rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The white bass and largemouth bass are still putting on a show at Stillhouse with 2-angler catches over 100 fish in a morning. We will likely drop back to a Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with a spinner and stinger hook going forward as the water cools and the fish slow down. There are plenty of largemouth bass and freshwater drum mixed in with the white bass in these same deep water areas. The shad-imitating 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab is the go-to bait for these fish.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Look for crappie on bridge pilings and structure in 15–20 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Bass can be caught with soft plastics on structure and brush in 8–15 feet of water. Bass will push up into coves and around docks, feeding on shad. Smaller fish are in 10-15 feet on structure with slabs, swimbaits or Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught with a swim jig, chatterbait, and spinnerbait on the bank in 1-6 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and can be caught in grass 5-10 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Finding grass around the lake is the ticket for bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working worms and flukes around any water vegetation have been the most productive. The outlet will always produce some bass too.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been excellent for big largemouth, especially when the sun is shining. Bass have started to move out from the backs of creeks and are starting to congregate at the mouths of main creek channels. Windy, sunny banks and retaining walls are good bets for black bass. On warm, sunny days, small shad pattern flies might produce bass around submerged vegetation.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite is slow with square bill crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits on long points or pond dams in 3-6 feet of water. Crappie fishing is excellent in the main river channel timber and lower third of the lake in 30-50 feet of water catching crappie 6-28 feet down. Fish are very healthy with big black crappie being caught on jigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: A few fish can be pulled right off the bottom by bouncing a slab. Crappie fishing remains slow with live minnows or jigs around brush piles and the 380 bridge may be the best bet to catch a few.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.50 pounds are slow on Tsunami 1/2 ounce jigs in Juice Box or Hubbard Craw in 1-5 feet on the ledges, or with crankbaits off the rocks in the deep pockets, 3-8 feet. Crappie are slow on white or black and chartreuse jigs and some off shore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Throwing jigs and shaky heads with trick worms, die those tails, around those rock piles will catch a pile of bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Cast rattle traps, Spoons, Umbrella Rigs, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 7-15 feet under bridge pylons, hidden brush piles throughout the lake or under docks. Crappie fisherman have been moving spot to spot finding limits. Lots of crappies in the 7-9 inch range. Limits of crappie will happen but you may catch a lot of small ones getting to your limit.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent for numbers of fish with an occasional bass to 8 pounds. Largemouth bass are good on crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good from up shallow to off shore on structure or schooling on shad. Crappie finding them in 13-22 feet close or in structure with jigs and minnows. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them, as well as casting swim baits or crank baits when schooled up.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been excellent for big largemouth, especially when the sun is shining. Bass have started to move out from the backs of creeks and are starting to congregate at the mouths of main creek channels.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White Bass are fair, look for birds working or schools of bait on the main lake and in mid-depths on chartreuse and white slabs or paddle tail swim baits. Crappie are being caught on deeper structure and cover using larger profile baits and also spider rigging open water.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The best bass bite is around big timber near channels and drop offs in 4-7 feet with chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, square bill crankbaits, Viper XP jigs, or Texas Rigs with creature baits. Black bass are slow in 5-10 feet of water with Clousers with a sinking tip line are your best bet. Small streamers and top water patterns might catch active bass in creeks on warm days. You can find big numbers of black crappie at the base of shallow trees in 12-18 feet in the mid lake areas. Sometimes you will find white crappie in the same trees suspended halfway down. The black crappie are higher on the trees off shore and the white crappie are further down on the trees. We have seen some bigger crappie…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair as anglers continue to wait for crappie to move to winter patterns on deep structures. Bass up to 9 pounds can be caught with a shallow crankbait or spinnerbait on rocky structure on the south side.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught in vegetation with crankbaits and Texas rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush piles in about 15 ft of water. Bass are shallow on rocky banks good on crank baits and spinner baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: The bigger sand bass have been more north between City Beach to Mallard Pointe and are good on slabs and 3-inch grubs fished on a �¼ ounce jig head. Largemouth bass are also good in numbers feeding with the sand bass near main lake points. Largemouth bass are good to 6 pounds slowing working soft plastics. Some good largemouth bass are also being caught in the river working laydowns. Crappie action is good on timber with small jigs fished from in town north to the Peninsula Subdivision.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are fair on jigs fished on the bottom in open water from 12-20 feet deep.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are tight to the shorelines close to cypress trees on warmer days, then seem to be a bit deeper on docks and structure on the colder days. Crappie are decent in east and west fork holding tight to structure around 14 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught on brush with minnows and jigs. Bass can be caught on Texas rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on the bank, docks, or on brush with soft plastics, and suspended fish with minnow style baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good in the hydrilla with swimbaits, chatterbaits, lipless crankbaits and senkos. Crappie are fair to good with minnows and Bobby Garland jigs in 15-25 feet around brush piles and existing timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on artificials. Crappie are fair with artificial baits and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in 12-18 feet of water Carolina rigs, dropshots or deep diving, trick worms or white and chartreuse worms. Crappie are excellent in 12-15 feet of water and standing timber with ⅛-1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: In any case, we still have some bass that are being seen in deeper water in larger groups.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. It is also important to slow down your retrieve this time of year to trigger these lethargic winter bass. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles using minnows. The occasional largemouth bass catch when crappie fishing.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: A couple of bass to 7 pounds on Alabama Rig near Gatlin Creek and in front of the dam. Crappie are fair in deeper trees along the main river channel in front of Elm Creek. Some crappie to 2 pounds reported. White bass slow on slabs suspended over River channels in front of the dam.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with very few reports of bites.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshot and small swimbaits in 16-20 feet of water. Crappie are poor on small white jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow to fair in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass are moving up with the lake level rising. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass on live bait and slabs.25-45 feet on deep water humps. Crappie are in 15-25 feet on brush piles and small patches of structure, minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair with a few reports of catches being made on slabs fished on the bottom in 25 feet of water off Pelican Island and main lake points.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing shad in the shallows and off points. When you can find grass on the south end there is usually a bass that can be caught on crankbaits. Crappie and white bass are moving in the river channel.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are slow on jigs and minnow over brush 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are slow on slow moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good off docks and concrete submerged structures and the crappie house. Bass are slow with very few reports from anglers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The white bass and largemouth bass are still putting on a show at Stillhouse with 2-angler catches over 100 fish in a morning still possible. Then drop back to a Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with spinner and stinger hook going forward as the water cools and the fish slow down. There are plenty of largemouth bass and freshwater drum mixed in with the white bass in these same deep water areas. The shad-imitating 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab is the go-to bait for these fish.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow with electronics to locate brush and structure in 15–20 feet of water, where fish will be holding tight to the brush. Bass fishing is fair as the water temperatures drop fish are becoming more active around midday along structure and main lake points. Some deadsticking action with a 4-5 inch weighted fluke, but the best action is on slabs in 32-60 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with shallow fish coming on rattle traps, swim jigs and swim baits. Mid range bass are in 8-14 feet with crankbaits and Texas rigs. The deeper bass bite has been hit-and-miss, but the forecasted cold weather should improve this bite.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are chasing shad in the backs of coves and cuts near deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with mostly smaller sized catches in deeper water on structure.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 20-25 feet of water. Bass are slow on trick worms and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are good in the crappie house on jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White Bass are fair, look for birds working or schools of bait on the main lake and in mid-depths on chartreuse and white slabs or paddle tail swim baits. Crappie are being caught on deeper structure and cover using larger profile baits and also spider rigging open water.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-35 feet on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on main lake points and ledges.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the grass in 5-10 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on structure with live minnows. Largemouth bass and smallmouth bass are shallow around structure using chatterbaits and Texas rigged worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite is excellent. Spotted bass schooling around the dam has slowed. Windy, sunny banks and retaining walls are good bets for black bass. On warm, sunny days, small shad pattern flies might produce bass around submerged vegetation.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow on points with grass, and the bite improves to fair in the bushes with spinnerbaits and rage swimmers in 3-6 feet. Crappie fishing is excellent in the main river channel timber and lower third of the lake in 30-50 feet of water catching crappie 6-28 feet down. Fish are very healthy with big black crappie being caught on jigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish have been good along rock lines on cheese bait bass and are fair along weed lines.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: A slab may coax a fish or two in the boat. Crappie have been slow but should be picking up as the water clears. Largemouth bass are fair on flat billed crankbaits and swim baits.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.23 pounds are fair on Tsunami �½ ounce jigs in 1-5 feet of water and Hags Hurricane Bladed jigs in the grass and weeds. Crappie are slow on white or black and chartreuse jigs and some offshore brush piles. White bass are slow on crankbaits and slabs scattered around the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Beginning to see crappie anglers out here more, and the white bass are running better.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent along grass edges with chatterbaits, crankbaits, and really whatever your favorite lure is. White bass are good in 30-50 with white or silver slabs spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hitting minnows in 30 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good up shallow and offshore on structure and shad schools. Crappie are in 13-22 feet of water close or in structure. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them, as well as casting swimbaits or crankbaits when schooled up.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The early morning bass bite is slow, but moving baits work around ditches and small creeks. Black bass are slow in 5-10 feet of water with Clousers with a sinking tip line are your best bet. Small streamers and top water patterns might catch active bass in creeks on warm days. You can find big numbers of black crappie at the base of shallow trees in 12-18 feet in the mid lake areas. Sometimes you will find white crappie in the same trees suspended halfway down. The black crappie are higher on the trees off shore and the white crappie are further down on the trees. We have seen some bigger crappie in the 2.5 pound range being caught so the winter time big fish season has arrived.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good relating to deep water structures near the outlet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush good on minnows. Bass are in shallow water good on moving vibrating baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass and white bass fishing is good on the lower ends on live bait, slabs and jigs worked on channel ledges from the dam to Decordova Estates Subdivision. Largemouth bass are good in numbers and can be caught mixed in with the striped bass and sand bass. Bigger largemouth bass are good on main lake points on soft plastics. Some good largemouth bass reports in the river near Tin Top working laydowns. Crappie action is good on submerged timber from the 377 bridges north to Hunter Park. Some good crappie are also being caught in the river on small jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Some fish are stacking in deep water and can be caught on slabs with a stinger hook.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Small bass are active in shallow areas relating to vegetation and structure.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are great chasing schooling shad and on the drop off by main channels. Crappie are in 10-14 feet of water roaming around and tight to structure.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught on brush with minnows and jigs. Bass can be caught on rattletraps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 20-30 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie need a bigger profile bait to zone in on. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been getting them. Expect to catch a couple black bass in your journey to the Blackwater. Black bass are still strong on white and chartreuse spinnerbaits with a half of a zoom motor oil worm as the trailer in1-5 feet on rocks or concrete. Texas rig and bass jigs are pulling them out of 15-20 feet deep brush piles. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows in 12-16 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good in grass on the lower end with red rattle traps, weightless senkos and chatterbaits. Some bass are still in 8-15 feet of water in the brush piles. Bass are good working docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and flukes.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are slow on humps and points in 15-28 feet of water with slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 6-26 feet of water. Bass are slow, with the most consistent bite in 2-6 feet of water slowly dragging soft plastics on a Texas rig or Ned rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Catching all fish on Ducktracker slabs and Texas teasers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the hydrilla with spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, swimbaits, rattletraps and senkos. Crappie fair in 10-25 feet fishing brush and timber with minnows and Bobby Garland screamer colored jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow in 14 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being seen in deeper water in larger groups hovering just off the bottom so a dropshot has been working well. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs and small swimbaits 15 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on 1/16 ounce chartreuse or white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services Report by Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass slow to 6 lb. Starting to see big schools of thread fin on Main Lake with bass following. Bass till shallow with ChatterBait and brush and 5 ft or less. Crappie are fair on Main Lake trees in 30 plus foot. Minnows best butt a lot of crappie on small jigs pink or silver.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass fishing is fair, look for birds and bait near the Pelican Island area and main lake points and keep a slab tied on.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. Crappie are slow over brush in 8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Black bass are slow on moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good off docks and concrete submerged structures and the crappie house. Bass are surfacing on shallow points near reeds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has been coming on strong. I have had numerous fish over 6 pounds showing up as bycatch when I am white bass fishing, and those targeting largemouth are doing very well working 5/8 ounce and 3/4 ounce. White Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs on bottom by both snap-jigging and by slowly raising them upwards after getting the attention of bottom-dwelling fish and watching their response on LiveScope.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and the bite is becoming stronger as the water temperature continues to cool. Bass are good in grass, shallow boat docks, and bluff walls with red rattle traps, weightless senkos and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair under the boat houses with minnows. Bass are slow on trick worms and crankbaits.
